messages:
maya: quick sync 10: partner proxy integration surfaced a confusion: console shows usage under the partner project but billing charge landed on the proxy org. that breaks our cost dashboards. any ideas?
owen: yeah this popped up in the proxy PoC. the token exchange step drops the original origin claim so downstream only sees the proxy identity.
lee: so the exchange binary mints a short-lived token without copying the `org`/`project` claims?
maya: correct. exchange returns sub tokens with `iss=proxy` and no `origin` claim. routing and quota use claims, so it attributes to proxy.
sam: short-term we could shadow-add an `x-origin` header at the proxy and have routing consult it just for observability. long-term we need a secure provenance mechanism.
kevin: can't accept plain headers for billing. forged headers = billing fraud. we need authenticity: either signed origin JWT or a trusted exchange-id with server-side mapping.
own: right. two safe patterns: signed-origin claim (partners sign origin with their key, we verify), or exchange-id mapping held by auth-proxy (exchange-id -> origin) checked by routing tier.
lee: signed origins remove the extra cache lookup but require partners to manage signing keys and rotate them. operational burden might slow adoption.
maya: mapping approach lets us roll out without partner changes. exchange service records mapping during token issue. routing layer does a tiny lookup. if cache hit, attribute correctly. if miss, fall back to current behavior and log.
sam: but quota enforcement requires immediate truth. delayed mapping only helps post-fact billing. we need request-time project for quota throttles.
kevin: we can keep quota decision conservative while in canary: continue enforcing on proxy identity but track a "would-have" quota using inferred origin. then later flip enforcement once mapping reliability is high.
own: ops impact: introduce a high-throughput cache with TTL ~5m and write-through on token exchange. expect high hit rates for steady clients. benchmark needed.
lee: console UX: add a Usage column "Inferred origin (exchange-id)" and a Reconciliation widget showing weekly discrepancy. tooltips explain confidence and that mapping is provisional during rollout.
maya: rollout plan suggestion: phase 1 - telemetry only for 14 days with 1% sampling, show reconciliation metrics; phase 2 - enable exchange-id mapping in routing for canary partner in us-west-2 with sample_rate 10% and monitor cache miss/latency; phase 3 - pilot signed-origin with one partner if they prefer no extra cache dependency; phase 4 - enable for all partners once SLA metrics satisfied.
kevin: telemetry counters I'll add: `auth.exchange.lookup_requested`, `auth.exchange.lookup_hit`, `auth.exchange.lookup_miss`, `auth.exchange.lookup_latency_ms`, and `auth.reconciliation.delta_pct`. will create a Grafana board.
sam: canary specifics: partner org id = P-42, region = us-west-2, sampling = 10% for 72h, alert if reconciliation delta > 3% or cache miss > 2% sustained for 15m.
own: I'll prototype a memory-backed LRU cache plus redis fallback. plan to measure p50/p99 lookup latency.
lee: on the console, also add a small help bubble "Why might billed org differ?" with recommended steps for partners. reduces support noise.
maya: security note: lock logs so exchange mappings are only in secure audit logs. avoid exposing project names or any PII. only show ids.
kevin: agree. also add a digest metric for daily reconciled-token-count per partner.
own: integration task list: implement cache API, add feature flag `auth.exchange.origin_map` default=false, emit mapping events, and ensure circuit-breaker if lookup downstream fails.
sam: ops/playbook: rollback if reconciliation delta spikes >5% or lookup latencies push request p95 above 100ms.
auth-bot: rolling deploy triggered: svc-auth-exchange v3.2.0 -> canary us-west-2 (1/4).
maya: thanks team. I'll gather these into a short rollout doc and ping partner success. :thumbsup:
